match.reason: The bank point covers the benefits and costs of inequality, but the new point asks how different groups (households, workers, businesses and governments) view inequality, weighing fairness, incentives and the cost of support, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Views on inequality
card: Different groups see inequality in different ways. There is no single correct view, because each group weighs fairness, incentives and cost differently.
Households and workers
Lower income households may see large gaps as unfair and want more support. Some workers see higher pay for hard work or skill as a fair reward.
Businesses
Owners may value rewards for effort and risk, since the chance of higher income can give people an incentive to work and invest. Many also want customers to have enough income to buy their goods.
Governments
Governments weigh fairness against the cost of support. Spending on welfare and services has to be paid for by taxes or borrowing, and high taxes may weaken incentives to work.
draft.remember: Each group weighs fairness, incentives to work and the cost of support in its own way.

a.q: A government hesitates to raise welfare payments. Which concern is it most likely weighing?
opts: The cost of support paid for by taxes or borrowing
The fairness of rewarding hard work with higher pay
The wish of businesses to attract more customers
The size of inheritances passed on to children
a.why: Governments must fund welfare through taxes or borrowing, so cost is a real limit. Rewarding hard work is a view held by some workers and owners, not the cost concern in this case.
a.clue: Someone has to pay for welfare payments.

b.q: Priya owns a small bakery in Ballarat and argues that higher pay for skilled bakers is fair. Which idea is she mainly relying on?
opts: Reward for effort and skill gives an incentive to work
Large income gaps are unfair and need more support
Government spending on welfare should always rise
Inequality has no effect on how people view fairness
b.why: Priya sees higher pay as a reward that encourages people to build skills and work hard. The second option is a view more often held by lower income households, so it does not match her argument.
b.clue: She links pay to effort and skill.

a.best: The cost of support paid for by taxes or borrowing

b.best: Reward for effort and skill gives an incentive to work

problems.detail: Why (b) refers to 'the second option' as the lower-income households' view, but options are shuffled. As shown, the second option is 'Government spending on welfare should always rise', not 'Large income gaps are unfair and need more support'. The why should name the option by its content.

The distractor 'Government spending on welfare should always rise' uses 'always', which the card never supports. Together with the illogical 'Inequality has no effect on how people view fairness', this leaves the right option easy to pick by elimination.
